doc.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026

title: Playing for the King of Morocco
summary: On a flight to Morocco he talked with a man named Mohammed who turned out to be the king's son, now King Mohammed.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You played for some royalty. I was looking at your thing, the King of Morocco and the royal family of The Netherlands.

Yeah it’s an interesting story about going to Morocco to play for the king. I was on the flight and they flew us in business class, and there were three of us sitting together. The guy next to me was from Morocco and we were speaking. And there was a guy who was with him who was just really quiet. You know he introduced me to him but he never said anything for the whole flight. And we were talking. His name was Mohammed. And we were – nice guy man, we talked the whole way man, you know, fun you know. And then we got there and the king’s personal security came to make sure we were okay, but this guy Mohammed, he didn’t have to pull out any documents, he went, he and the king’s personal security guy did the two cheek kiss and he walked on through. Damn. And then when I saw the king’s family I saw the way they looked and I said oh my God this is the king’s son. So he is now King Mohammed.
Oh man. I’m sure you were thinking back like gee, what did I say to him. Wow that’s a great experience.
